text:
anya: Quick sync — proposing a kernel switching policy for attention kernels across regions. TL;DR: prefer flashv3 on H100 when p95 > 120ms OR cost/token > $0.0009 in us-west1; otherwise stick with Triton vendor kernels for stability. Thoughts? :thinking:

mike: Can you post the raw numbers? curious about p50 vs p95 and token throughput tradeoffs.

sara: We saw a weird regression yesterday in eu-west1 for q8 quant that only shows up at p99 — worth calling out.

anya: Sure, summary from yesterday's sweep (Llama-2-13B q8 / seq=2048):
- us-west1 (H100, flashv3): p50=45ms, p95=130ms, tokens/s=6800, cost/token=$0.00085
- us-west1 (H100, triton-vendor): p50=50ms, p95=115ms, tokens/s=6400, cost/token=$0.00081
- eu-west1 (H100, flashv3): p50=48ms, p95=175ms, p99=320ms, tokens/s=6600
- eu-west1 (A100, triton): p50=70ms, p95=240ms, tokens/s=4200

lee: So flashv3 wins on throughput and p50 generally, but tails are worse in eu-west1. Could be firmware/PCI topology or kernel-vendor mismatch.

jonah: Did we test flashv2 as well? I want to see whether v3's new fused kernels are causing the p99 spikes.

anya: Yes — flashv2 on eu-west1 H100: p50=49ms, p95=160ms, p99=280ms, tokens/s=6500. So v3 worsened tail by ~10-15% in that region.

mike: Hmm. Might be NUMA/PCIe skew. Also note our batching distribution in eu-west1 is heavier (more mix of long seqs). That exposes kernel fragility.

anya: Proposal for policy (config snippet):
```yaml
kernel_policy:
  - condition:
      region: eu-west1
      model_tags: ["llama2-13b", "q8"]
      p99_threshold_ms: 300
    action: use_triton_fallback
    hysteresis: 0.10 # 10% buffer before switching back
  - condition:
      gpu: h100
      p95_threshold_ms: 120
      cost_per_token_threshold: 0.0009
    action: prefer_flashv3
    canary: 5%
```

sara: Love the hysteresis. We should add a quantization-specific flag — q8 tends to affect memory layout and kernel path.

anya: Good call. I'll add a quant flag. Also proposing automatic canary rollout: 5% traffic to flashv3, monitor p95 and quality drift for 2 hours, then ramp.

jonah: For quality drift, we need automated prompts set. Add eval hooks to block rollout if rouge-1 drops >0.7% on our prompt suite.

mike: Who owns the rollout? @lee or infra? I can help with automation.

lee: Infra runs the canary automation but we need eng-ml to define thresholds. I'll implement the policy once thresholds are final.

anya: Additional notes: vendor kernels (triton) have lower tail in eu-west1 so fallback there is safer. But in us-west1 flashv3 gives the best cost/throughput so we prefer it by default.

benchbot: benchbot: sweep complete for 2026-11-04 03:12 UTC — attached chart link: https://internal/bench/runs/1856017001 (p50/p95/p99 + cost).

infra-bot: infra-bot: deployed kernel_policy v1.2 to staging; canary rollout endpoints created.

anya: Next steps: 1) add quant flag, 2) formalize p95/p99 thresholds per region, 3) run 4h canary with eval hooks. I'll open a PR with the YAML and perf dashboards.

mike: Sounds good. I'll own the canary automation. Tag me on the PR. :thumbsup:

sara: Also adding an action item to replicate eu-west1 hardware topology in our lab to debug p99 (PCIe/firwmware).

lee: Noted. If we can't reproduce, plan B is vendor support ticket with vendor kernels + flamegraphs.

anya: OK — I'll file the PR and ping this thread. Thanks everyone. :fire:

mike: Thanks — bookmarking the bench link now.

benchbot: benchbot: note — run-level metric: quality_eval/rouge1 change = -0.2% (within tolerance).
